My experience using Emergency Vets Glasgow has always been really positive and reassuring. The staff are incrediblely empathetic and patient. They are really accommodating. The vets are never in a rush to get you out. They've always gone above and beyond for the dogs I've brought in with me. The biggets pros of using this Out of Hours vets over Vets Now in Glasgow City centre is that their pricing is almost half of what you'll pay at Vets Now. An overnight stay with them is £500 odd, whereas at Vets Now its almost £1000. For pet owners who arent insured then this out of hours vets is the better option. The only con for me is that you have to pay at the time of treatment, you cannot do any direct claims to your pet insurance. This means I would need to have the funds first to get any treatment to then claim it back, which doesnt always work for me. If I don't have the funds on me then I need to use VetsNow instead despite the big price hike, because they accept direct insurance claims! With that aside, I do rate these guys really highly 👌

Called up to ask about our dog getting seen and was told that it’s £180 upfront for the appointment and then depending on the outcome and treatment we would need to pay for what ever treatment is needed upfront. Why have insurance and you can’t use it at a vets. How is anyone supposed to be able to afford 5 grand for instance just laying around the house.
The whole point is to get help for your pet and the insurance company supports with the rest.
Avoid this place if you value your pets as this is simply a money grabbing service

I can't thank Nick and the team more for all they did to save our Hudson. Although he tragically passed, they treated Hudson and us with the utmost compassion and dignity. You can tell how much they care for the animals. I think the lovely technician was called Shannon, even stayed late to look after us. And I didn't get the other technician's name but she made sure Hudson looked like his usual handsome self and took the time to take pawprints and fur clippings as keepsakes while reassuring us in our grief. What these amazing people do is not easy and I thank them so so much for their care and compassion.

We brought our dog here in an emergency after she went into severe heart failure. Her lungs and heart were filled with fluid and she was struggling to breathe. She has mitral valve disease that, unfortunately, had been completely overlooked and untreated by our regular vet.

Dr Nick and the whole team were incredibly attentive and compassionate with our dog. He took the time to explain everything clearly, including the reality of her condition and the limited time she may have left because the disease had not been treated properly from the beginning.

Yes, this place is expensive. Even being one of the more affordable emergency options in Glasgow, emergency veterinary care is still very costly. But the care, professionalism, and kindness our dog received here were truly exceptional.

They saved her life, and gave us a little more time with her. We will always be grateful for that.

Visited Emergency Vets Glasgow when my dog, Frost had a suspected intestinal blockage on a Saturday night. I was advised to come in immediately and was seen relatively quickly on arrival.

Frost received a full work-up including a physical exam, blood tests, ultrasound, and X-rays. Once the obstruction was identified, surgery was carried out promptly.

What really stood out was the level of communication throughout. Every step was clearly explained, from what they were assessing in the bloods (such as hydration status) to the surgical approach and stitching technique used. Both the operating surgeon and the vet who discharged Frost referenced current research and explained how this informed their decisions, which gave me a lot of confidence in the care provided.

Despite this being a very stressful situation, I always felt informed and supported. I was given the information I needed to make decisions, without feeling overwhelmed, which helped me trust the team and feel reassured that I was making the best decisions for Frost.

The surgery was successful, and I’m incredibly grateful for the speed, professionalism, and compassion shown throughout. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this practice in an emergency and would happily use them again.

The only drawback is that payment is required upfront, even if you have insurance. I was fortunately able to cover the cost, but I appreciate this may not be possible for everyone. That said, the process was made as smooth as possible because the receptionist took my insurance details at the time of payment and said their team will handle the insurance request, which removed a lot of the admin on my side. And unlike my regular vet, there was no additional fee for this service, which I really appreciated.

I want to express my sincere gratitude to the entire team at EVG for the exceptional care Penny received last night and today. Special thanks to Kirsten, Matt, Chris, and the lovely man at the front desk (apologies for not catching his name) for their kindness, professionalism, and dedication.

We brought my granddad’s dog, Penny, in after she deteriorated following a vet visit earlier in the day. The team went above and beyond, providing not only outstanding medical care but also keeping us updated on Penny’s condition throughout the evening. They were incredibly transparent about the treatment options and costs, which was especially important as Penny isn’t insured.

The suspected diagnosis was idiopathic pericarditis, and thanks to the expertise and compassion of the team, Penny is now home, recovering well, and has finally found her waggy tail again. I truly believe she wouldn’t have received this level of care anywhere else. Every member of the team we interacted with was not only knowledgeable but also down-to-earth and empathetic, making a very stressful situation much easier to navigate.

We also want to give a huge thank you to the nurses and care assistants working behind the scenes, who we didn’t get the chance to meet but who no doubt played a vital role in Penny’s care and recovery. Your work may not always be visible to owners, but it absolutely makes all the difference.

I wouldn’t hesitate to bring a pet here again should they ever need emergency care. Thank you again to everyone at EVG — your care has made a world of difference to Penny and our family.

My dog was admitted here for overnight care when she became ill with hemorrhagic gastroenteritis. Most veterinary surgeries don't have out-of-hours facilities, and pets in Glasgow that require care after their surgery closes, will most likely be admitted here overnight or to Vets Now at Charing Cross. I only learned this when my dog required emergency care and I wish I'd understood more about the process sooner. It involved me transporting a very sick dog with a life-threatening illness between surgeries - a situation that with hindsight seems neither practical nor safe but was the only option I had at the time.

Upon arriving at Emergency Vets Glasgow (EVG) with my dog for her first night in their care, I was immediately asked to pay an upfront fee of over £495. Initially, everything seemed fine; there was a consultation with the vet on shift and I had no issues at that stage. My dog was then taken by the veterinary nurse to have blood drawn. While waiting at reception, I was alarmed to hear my dog screaming loudly from a consulting room while she was left with the nurse. When I expressed concern, I was told it was due to difficulty in obtaining blood, although she had shown no signs of distress beforehand and had already had blood taken that day.

I was instructed to pick her up first thing in the morning and return her to her regular veterinary practice for further monitoring. When I arrived to collect her, I was asked to speak with the vet first. The vet explained that, during the night, my dog had been lying on her side with an IV line, which had slipped, causing the fluids to leak under her skin, resulting in a massive swelling on her side. Adding to this distress, the veterinary nurse appeared in the hallway and dragged my dog between consulting rooms for unclear reasons before handing her to me without a word or even making eye contact. Even considering the exhaustion of a night shift, this behavior demonstrated an unacceptable lack of professionalism.

I remained calm throughout my dealings with the team at EVG, as my focus was on my very sick dog, but I was deeply upset by my experience. I had trusted them to monitor my dog. This was the primary reason she was in their care.

The swelling issue was downplayed, and I was told that the veterinary nurse at my dog's usual practice would likely use a warm compress and massage to reduce the swelling, with the fluid dispersing naturally. I was assured the fluid did not contain pain relief and was "mainly just water."

However, I later discovered this issue can be far more serious if the fluid includes pain relief, as it can be fatal. And upon reviewing my dog's records, I learned she had been administered pain relief through the leaking IV. This was documented in the notes sent to her regular vet and in the paperwork for the insurance claim.

I have waited to reflect on the incident before writing this review. It was, and still is, deeply upsetting to think about. My dog was a rescue puppy who had already been through a great deal before I got her. I also wanted to ensure my insurance claim was settled and that my dog was moved to a vet with on-site out-of-hours facilities. While the situation warrants a formal complaint to the RCVS, I chose instead to leave a review to help other pet owners make informed decisions—if they have the time to seek alternatives.

Accidents and mistakes can happen, but the attempt to downplay the seriousness of this incident is concerning. Treating people and their  pets with honesty and respect should be the bare minimum. I am simply grateful that my dog survived.

I have purposely not named the individual veterinary nurse or vet involved in this complaint to maintain their privacy.
